decisions.reason: Section 11.1 sets commencement at first use or acceptance, whichever is earlier, and duration through the Order Form term or termination under Section 11 (line 112). The current rule captures that term commencement and duration; it does not grant a separate use right.

Section 11.2 permits Customer to cease use and terminate when no Order Forms are in effect, subject to outstanding payment obligations and with no refund of prepaid fees (line 114). The current rule captures the same condition and payment duty.

Section 11.3 gives Mistral AI the discretionary right to immediately suspend or terminate account or product access on the listed alternative grounds, including End User access (line 116). The current rule captures that right and grounds; its prohibition modality is an inaccurate representation of the right, but the candidate itself does not identify a distinct Customer activity restriction to add.

Section 11.3 says Customer may appeal a suspension or termination by contacting support (line 116). This is a procedural appeal permission, not an activity concerning an allowed artifact object; representing it as permission to Use a product would confuse an appeal right with product-use permission.

Section 11.4 states that Customer’s right to use the Products immediately ceases on termination or expiration (line 118). The current rule captures that trigger and cessation; the candidate’s ancillary refrain duty is likewise expressed there.

Section 11.4 requires payment of outstanding Fees, unpaid invoices, and other charges incurred through termination (line 118). The current rule includes that same payment duty as an obligation item. Its separate use-cessation condition does not negate coverage of the ancillary payment obligation.

Section 11.4 requires Customer that desires an export from its Customer Account to complete it before terminating the account, while warning that export may not be possible afterward (line 118). The current rule captures that conditional export duty and object.

Section 12.2 states Mistral AI collects and processes Customer Personal Data as controller in accordance with its privacy policy, whose URL may change (line 125). The current rule records this same processing and external-policy reference without inventing the policy’s missing requirements.

Section 12.3 makes the DPA applicable between the Parties if Customer uses Mistral Infrastructure and Mistral AI processes Personal Data on Customer’s behalf (line 127). The current rule captures that condition and the missing external DPA without inferring its substantive terms.

Section 13.1 permits Mistral AI to update the Terms and the specified related terms, subject to Section 13’s procedures (line 130). The current rule captures the update authority and procedural condition.
Section 13.3 makes material updates effective 30 days after notice (line 134). The current rule captures that timing; the same source passage also states the separate immediate-effect alternatives.

Section 13.3 makes updates effective immediately upon posting when non-material, made for legal compliance, or made to address a material security risk (line 134). The current rule preserves those alternative grounds and posting requirement.

Section 13.4 makes stopping use and terminating before the update’s effective date the sole and exclusive remedy for disagreement, with termination effective on that date (line 136). The current rule captures that conditional response and timing.

Section 13.4 says continued use on or after the effective date constitutes acceptance of the updated Terms (line 136). The current rule captures this alternative consequence and does not turn it into a duty to continue using the Products.

Section 14.1 requires covered notices and communications to be written and specifies the recipient-dependent routes and addressing instructions (line 139). The current rule captures the form, applicable channels, and scope of the requirement.

Section 14.2 restricts Customer’s assignment or transfer of rights and subcontracting of obligations to a third party absent Mistral AI’s prior written consent (line 141). The current rule captures the same actor, conduct, object, and consent condition; this is contract assignment, not a Product sublicense.

Section 14.2 gives Mistral AI a right to assign, transfer, or subcontract to an affiliate without Customer’s prior written consent (line 141). This is a contract-assignment permission, not an allowed activity concerning an artifact; representing it as Sublicense of the OriginalArtifact would misstate the provision.

Section 14.4 bars either Party from using the other’s name, logos, or marks without that other Party’s written pre-approval for each use; email suffices (line 145). The current rule captures the reciprocal actors, objects, and approval condition.

Section 14.5 provides that neither Party may bind the other or incur obligations on its behalf without prior written consent (line 147). The current rule captures the same reciprocal prohibition and consent condition.
